title: Chinese Singer Liu Yuning Expands His Musical World With New Music & Cross-Cultural Collaborations
summary: "JUMP" sees Liu Yuning teaming up with J Balvin on a track that blends rock with traditional Chinese instruments.
contentText:
As part of Billboard China and QQ Music’s recent global campaign, Chinese singer Liu Yuning reached a new milestone with his latest single “JUMP,” earning a series of featured promotional opportunities.

The track sees Liu Yuning teaming up with J Balvin on a cross-cultural collaboration that blends rock with traditional Chinese instruments, including the pipa, guzheng, erhu and Tang-style drums. Combined with Ning’s energetic rap delivery, “JUMP” — which interpolates Van Halen’s Billboard Hot 100 -topping hit from 1983 — creates a seamless meeting point between Eastern and Western musical influences.

At the same time, Ning is steadily unveiling his long-awaited second solo album, Liu Yuning’s , his first full-length project in five years. Rather than releasing the album all at once, he has chosen a track-by-track rollout, with nine songs available so far.

Among them is “Not Too Late,” released earlier this year, which offers one of the album’s most intimate moments. Written and produced by singer/songwriter Penny Tai, the warm rock ballad reflects on the emotional weight that comes with life in the spotlight. Its lyrics capture feelings of exhaustion, misunderstanding and self-doubt, while ultimately delivering a message of resilience and hope. Instead of dwelling on hardship, the song becomes an invitation to rediscover inner strength.

The album’s more recent releases, “Door” and “I Want,” showcase two contrasting emotional landscapes. “Door” turns inward, pairing restrained vocals with an enveloping arrangement to convey isolation, uncertainty and quiet introspection. In contrast, “I Want” opens outward. Driven by bright guitar lines and soaring vocals, the song releases the emotional tension built throughout its companion track, highlighting Ning’s dynamic vocal control and expressive range as it moves from vulnerability toward clarity and liberation.

Beyond his solo work, Ning continues to establish himself as one of China’s most in-demand OST vocalists. He has recently contributed songs to several popular television dramas, demonstrating remarkable versatility across genres and storytelling.

For Yu Ting Yao , “Seeing Mountains and Rivers” balances epic grandeur with emotional depth, echoing the series’ sweeping historical narrative. In The Road to Splendor , his song “A Promise” takes the idea of keeping one’s word as its emotional core. Backed by his deeply expressive vocals, the track captures the resilience and sense of responsibility of people trying to hold on to their principles in turbulent times. Meanwhile, “Borrow a Little Light From Ordinary Days” feels like a bedside lamp in a complicated world, using understated musical language to celebrate the quiet heroism found in everyday life.

From the deeply personal reflections of his second album to his emotionally resonant work for film and television, Liu Yuning continues to expand the scope of his artistry. With each new release, he is building a musical universe that is unmistakably his own.
